brief: Egypt: Lulu Group opened a hypermarket of about 106,000 sq ft in Obour City, Cairo, and its chairman said more Egypt projects are in the pipeline (Amwal Al Ghad, 16 Nov; Daily News Egypt, 17 Nov).

Türkiye: ZEISS opened its first Türkiye Vision Center at İstanbul AVM, the shopping centre in the İstanbul Finance Centre, which was reported opening on 24 Sep and has since added MANGO and MediaMarkt (Mall Report, 17 Nov).

Kazakhstan: Asia Park in Astana made a net profit of 1.4 billion tenge in January to September on 2.6 billion tenge of rental income, figures its Kazakhstan Stock Exchange issuer page matches (Kursiv, 17 Nov).
UAE: Alef Group's 06 Mall in Sharjah will carry a façade screen for 3D advertising from CITIX MENA, with smartboards across its Al Mamsha community (Campaign Middle East, 17 Nov).

Events and AI: Türkiye's AYD holds its 17th Shopping Economy Summit in Istanbul on 8 Dec, the second day of RCM Jeddah, and Daydream launched a fashion agent that can check out for shoppers (Mall Report; TechCrunch, 17 Nov).

findings.title: Lulu opens a hypermarket of about 106,000 sq ft in Obour City, Cairo, and says more Egypt projects are under way
findings.summary: Lulu Group has opened a hypermarket of about 106,000 sq ft in Obour City, Cairo Governorate, with groceries, fresh food, bakery, electronics, home appliances and fashion accessories, self-checkout counters and its own parking (Amwal Al Ghad, 16 Nov; Daily News Egypt, 17 Nov; both give the same size). It was opened by Hossam El Garrahi of Egypt's Internal Trade Development Authority, with the UAE ambassador to Egypt and Lulu chairman Yusuffali M.A. present. Yusuffali said several new Egypt projects are in the pipeline; neither report names a mall or project for the site, a store count or an investment figure.
findings.why: Lulu adds another large-format grocery anchor in Egypt, where hypermarkets underpin new community and regional centres, and says more openings are coming.

findings.entity: ZEISS Vision Center, İstanbul AVM (İstanbul Finans Merkezi)
findings.company: ZEISS; Beta Optik (ZEISS Vision Care distributor in Türkiye)
findings.title: ZEISS opens its first Türkiye Vision Center at İstanbul AVM, the new shopping centre in the İstanbul Finance Centre
findings.summary: ZEISS has opened Türkiye's first ZEISS Vision Center, an optical store built around ZEISS lenses and its VISUFIT 1000 fitting system, at İstanbul Alışveriş Merkezi (İstanbul AVM) in the İstanbul Finance Centre, Mall Report reported on 17 Nov in an item quoting Mustafa Kemal Köksal, chief executive of Beta Optik, ZEISS Vision Care's distributor in Türkiye. The item reads as a press release and gives no store size, opening day or operator. The centre was reported opening its doors on 24 Sep (Timeturk, 25 Sep); MANGO has since opened its 80th Türkiye store there, of more than 1,200 sq m (MANGO release, 8 Oct), and MediaMarkt a store with 925 sq m of sales area on 6 Nov (MediaMarkt release, 6 Nov).
findings.why: The İstanbul Finance Centre's shopping centre is trading and adding international tenants, and ZEISS's first Türkiye store is a candidate for the 2027 Directory's Retail Brands section.

findings.entity: Asia Park shopping and entertainment centre
findings.title: Astana's Asia Park makes 1.4 billion tenge net profit in nine months on 2.6 billion tenge of rental income
findings.summary: TOO Asia Park, which owns the Asia Park shopping and entertainment centre in Astana, made a net profit of 1.4 billion tenge in January to September 2026 on revenue of 2.6 billion tenge, all of it rental income, Kursiv reported on 17 Nov from the company's financial statements. Its issuer page on the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange, where it has three privately placed bond issues, shows net profit of 1,358,638 thousand tenge, operating income of 2,591,230 thousand tenge and total assets of 11,654,465 thousand tenge in the column dated 1 Oct 2026. Kursiv says Arcada Group (95%) and Arcada (5%), both of Karaganda and owned by entrepreneur Alexey Nefedov, hold the company, and that a reconstruction adding a business centre and offices is under way.
findings.why: Exchange-filed results for a Central Asian mall are rare: they confirm the owner of a listed directory property and show its rent-driven earnings ahead of a reconstruction that adds offices.

sources.outlet: Kazakhstan Stock Exchange (KASE), Asia Park issuer page (figures at 1 Oct 2026, read 18 Nov)

findings.title: Sharjah's 06 Mall will carry a façade screen for 3D advertising, with smartboards across Al Mamsha, from CITIX MENA
findings.summary: CITIX MENA will install 'Jumbo', a large-format digital screen for premium and naked-eye 3D campaigns, on the façade of Alef Group's 06 Mall in Sharjah, Campaign Middle East reported on 17 Nov. The rollout also adds roadside and pedestrian smartboards across Alef's Al Mamsha community, built on CITIX MENA's Citix Panel to show real-time information, widgets and brand messages that adapt to conditions. CITIX MENA, an urban technology company working in Sharjah, Dubai and Abu Dhabi, is offering the formats to brands, media agencies and retail partners; the report gives no screen size or go-live date.
findings.why: A community mall turning its façade and neighbourhood into sellable digital media is a GCC example of retail media income beyond rent.

findings.company: AYD (Alışveriş Merkezleri ve Yatırımcıları Derneği), with Alkaş
findings.title: Türkiye's shopping centre association AYD holds its 17th Shopping Economy Summit in Istanbul on 8 Dec
findings.summary: AYD, Türkiye's association of shopping centres and investors, will hold its 17th Shopping Economy Summit on Tuesday 8 Dec 2026 at Swissôtel The Bosphorus in Istanbul, organised with Alkaş and with Fiba Commercial Properties as main sponsor (Mall Report and AVM Dergi, 17 Nov). The programme covers economic resilience, global investment opportunities with Aamal Company chief executive Rashid Bin Ali Al Mansoori, the carbon economy after COP31, luxury retail with ECE Türkiye and Beymen Group, and governance in family companies, and Deputy Trade Minister Mahmut Gürcan is among the opening speakers. Akademetre Research will present the first results of a study of Gen Z and Gen Alpha consumers, and the day ends with the AYD No. 1 Brands awards.
findings.why: A peer association's flagship summit falls on 8 Dec, the second day of RCM Jeddah, and its study of Gen Z and Gen Alpha shoppers is worth obtaining for MECSR content.

findings.title: iSTYLE moves its Apple Premium Partner store at Abu Dhabi Mall to a larger unit
findings.summary: iSTYLE, an Apple Premium Partner backed by Midis Group, has moved its Abu Dhabi Mall store to a larger space laid out to Apple's latest retail concept, with interactive workshops, demonstrations and a full service centre, according to a report in Gulf News' corporate news section last updated on 12 Nov. Nicolas Daher, managing director retail at Midis Group, announced the move. The report gives no opening date, floor or store size.
findings.why: A tenant upgrade at one of Abu Dhabi's established regional malls, built around in-store service and workshops.

findings.title: Fashion start-up Daydream launches an AI stylist agent that can complete purchases with one-click checkout
findings.summary: Daydream, the fashion search start-up founded by Julie Bornstein, launched Daydream Agent on 17 Nov, TechCrunch reported. The agent remembers each shopper's style, fit and budget, tries items on virtually from an uploaded photo, plans outfits with a connected wardrobe and calendar, and tracks sales and brand drops with weekly updates; saved items go on a persistent 'clothing rack', and the agent can complete a purchase through one-click checkout. The report does not say how each purchase is approved or in which countries the agent is available.
findings.why: Another agent that shops across many brands' catalogues and checks out for the buyer, adding to the open question of how GCC fashion retailers and malls open product data and checkout to outside AI agents.

watch.note: No GCC bank, payment network or retailer had set rules to admit or block outside AI shopping agents by 18 Nov. New: Daydream's stylist agent can complete purchases through one-click checkout, without the report saying how each purchase is approved (TechCrunch, 17 Nov; see 18 Nov). Also: OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet lets its dots agents complete purchases with tokenised cards and Face ID or fingerprint approval for each purchase, first for some US Pro subscribers, and OpenAI published a Commerce Partner Playbook for retailers (TechCrunch, 13 Nov; see 16 Nov). Also: OpenAI's Businesses in ChatGPT lets companies claim their profiles and add product feeds, with Business Agents first for US online sellers (Reuters, 10 Nov; see 12 Nov). Also: CrediMax and Mastercard will explore agentic commerce for Bahrain merchants, starting with Mastercard's Agent Suite for Merchants (Mastercard, 4 Nov; see 10 Nov), and Zalando launched an agent that buys from other retailers inside its app (Reuters, 3 Nov; see 10 Nov). Earlier context: American Express's Intent Intelligence framework (13 Oct), Meta and Sierra's Personal Agent Protocol (14 Oct), Amazon and eBay blocking agents (16 Oct), Walmart's Agent Gateway (21 Oct), US banks restricting third-party agents (23 Oct), BCG's survey of large retailers (21 Oct, see 28 Oct), PYMNTS and Visa on UAE merchants' readiness (26 Oct), Meta's Muse (28 Oct), Home Depot's rules for agents (29 Oct), Retail Dive's holiday survey round-up (3 Nov), and Amazon's Alexa for Shopping for outside merchants (4 Nov) and text-to-shop test (6 Nov)
